Step 1: We use polynomial long division to divide \(x^6 - 3\) by \(x + 1\).

Step 2: Set up the division with \(x^6 - 3\) under the division symbol and \(x + 1\) outside.

Step 3: Divide the leading term of the dividend \(x^6\) by the leading term of the divisor \(x\), which gives \(x^5\). Write \(x^5\) above the division symbol.

Step 4: Multiply \(x^5\) by \(x + 1\) to get \(x^6 + x^5\). Subtract this from \(x^6 - 3\) to get \(-x^5 - 3\).

Step 5: Bring down \(-x^5 - 3\). Divide \(-x^5\) by \(x\) to get \(-x^4\). Write \(-x^4\) above the division symbol.

Step 6: Multiply \(-x^4\) by \(x + 1\) to get \(-x^5 - x^4\). Subtract this from \(-x^5 - 3\) to get \(x^4 - 3\).

Step 7: Bring down \(x^4 - 3\). Divide \(x^4\) by \(x\) to get \(x^3\). Write \(x^3\) above the division symbol.

Step 8: Multiply \(x^3\) by \(x + 1\) to get \(x^4 + x^3\). Subtract this from \(x^4 - 3\) to get \(-x^3 - 3\).

Step 9: Bring down \(-x^3 - 3\). Divide \(-x^3\) by \(x\) to get \(-x^2\). Write \(-x^2\) above the division symbol.

Step 10: Multiply \(-x^2\) by \(x + 1\) to get \(-x^3 - x^2\). Subtract this from \(-x^3 - 3\) to get \(x^2 - 3\).

Step 11: Bring down \(x^2 - 3\). Divide \(x^2\) by \(x\) to get \(x\). Write \(x\) above the division symbol.

Step 12: Multiply \(x\) by \(x + 1\) to get \(x^2 + x\). Subtract this from \(x^2 - 3\) to get \(-x - 3\).

Step 13: Bring down \(-x - 3\). Divide \(-x\) by \(x\) to get \(-1\). Write \(-1\) above the division symbol.

Step 14: Multiply \(-1\) by \(x + 1\) to get \(-x - 1\). Subtract this from \(-x - 3\) to get \(-2\).

Final answer: \boxed{x^5 - x^4 + x^3 - x^2 + x - 1 - \frac{2}{x+1}}
